title: Chunk Size (Textable, Numeric)
documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies the maximum number of tokens or characters in a single chunk when splitting documents for processing. Controls the granularity of content segmentation.

## When to use
Set this parameter on chunking or ingestion machines that split large documents before passing them to models with limited context windows. Smaller chunks increase retrieval precision; larger chunks preserve more context per segment.

## Notes
Valid range: 10–2000. Pair with [Chunk Overlap](https://capdag.com/browse/media:chunk-overlap;textable;numeric) to retain context across chunk boundaries, and with [Max Content Length](https://capdag.com/browse/media:max-content-length;textable;numeric) to ensure chunks fit within downstream limits.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
